title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 establishes that artificial intelligence cannot replace or perform the duties of licensed medical doctors. It requires that all medical care and diagnostic decisions be carried out by qualified human clinicians, ensuring accountability, patient safety, and adherence to professional standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 creates a legal framework for systematically assessing the safety, security, and potential harms of AI systems before they are deployed. It requires developers and organizations to conduct risk evaluations, document their findings, and submit reports to regulators so that AI products meet established safety standards before reaching the market.

title: To establish in the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency of the Department of Homeland Security a task force on artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy creates a task force at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) under the Department of Homeland Security to focus on artificial intelligence issues. The task force will also handle related responsibilities to support national cybersecurity and infrastructure protection.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 establishes comprehensive rules for how AI systems can be designed, used, and monitored to protect public safety, privacy, and fairness. It sets requirements for testing, transparency, user consent, and oversight to ensure AI technologies operate responsibly across all sectors.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act temporarily stops the building or opening of new data centers that are dedicated to artificial‑intelligence use.  It is intended to pause AI‑specific infrastructure growth while lawmakers evaluate its environmental, security, and regulatory implications.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes federal requirements for AI developers and operators to assess, report, and minimize their technology’s environmental footprint, including energy consumption and carbon emissions. It also creates incentives for green AI practices, sets standards for sustainable AI development, and provides oversight to ensure compliance with environmental goals.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act seeks to guide the development and use of artificial intelligence so that it directly benefits the American public, emphasizing responsible innovation, equitable access, and fair distribution of economic gains. The bill proposes safeguards to protect privacy, security, and workers' rights, while encouraging investment in AI research and ensuring that new technologies enhance, rather than displace, jobs across industries.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed law that would make learning about artificial intelligence a part of school curricula from kindergarten through high school. It aims to give students foundational AI knowledge, teach them how to use and think critically about AI, and provide teachers with training, resources, and fair access to technology so all schools can prepare students for an AI‑driven world.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a law designed to ensure that AI systems are safe, trustworthy, and built on reliable data. It sets standards for testing, documentation, and oversight of AI research so that new technologies can be responsibly developed and deployed.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 establishes guidelines and oversight to ensure that AI systems are developed and tested for safety, reliability, and transparency. It requires research institutions to follow standardized testing protocols, disclose methods, and report potential risks to federal regulators.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to set up a pilot program that uses AI to defend critical infrastructure from cyber threats. The program is intended to test AI technologies for improving the security of essential systems, with additional related objectives also noted.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to ensure that students in kindergarten through 12th grade receive comprehensive education about artificial intelligence. It establishes standards, resources, and training for teachers so that schools can effectively incorporate AI knowledge into curricula and prepare students for a future where AI is integral to daily life.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that sets rules for how the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs can use artificial intelligence to handle veterans’ benefits claims. It requires the VA to be transparent about AI decision‑making, ensure the technology is fair and accurate, and establish oversight to protect veterans’ rights.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to fully disclose and explain how it uses artificial intelligence in its programs and services, ensuring veterans and the public understand the purpose, benefits, and risks of AI tools. It sets standards for reporting, oversight, and accountability so that AI deployment in veteran care is transparent, ethical, and subject to regular review.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act seeks to boost public understanding of artificial intelligence by launching nationwide education and awareness initiatives. It establishes programs, resources, and partnerships to inform citizens about the benefits, risks, and responsible use of AI technologies.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution creates a Select Committee dedicated to Artificial Intelligence, establishing a formal body to oversee AI policy. The committee will advise lawmakers on AI-related issues and recommend legislative actions to ensure responsible development and use of AI.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate issued a resolution that highlights the importance of protecting religious freedom as it relates to the development and use of artificial intelligence. It also stresses the need for transparent AI systems and the consideration of authoritative texts in guiding their design and implementation.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating an Artificial Intelligence Safety Board to oversee the development and deployment of AI technologies, ensuring they meet safety standards and address potential risks. It also includes related provisions that support the board’s work, such as funding, reporting requirements, and coordination with existing agencies.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This act seeks to protect consumers from misleading AI practices by establishing clear rules for transparency and honesty. It requires companies to disclose when AI is used and how it affects users, ensuring that consumers can make informed decisions and avoid deceptive marketing.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress on how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report will give Congress oversight and insight into AI’s role in intelligence gathering within that legal framework.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 is designed to improve AI skills and knowledge among students and workers, ensuring that the U.S. workforce can keep pace with rapid technological change. It sets up federal grants to boost AI curriculum in schools and to provide training programs for employees in high‑growth AI sectors.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is designed to encourage the development and use of AI technologies that are open-source, ensuring they are built in a transparent and responsible manner. It sets out guidelines for collaboration, licensing, and the sharing of AI models so that innovation can grow while safeguarding user privacy and security.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to curb the practice of charging excessively high prices for AI products and services, and to prevent companies from engaging in wage manipulation within the AI industry. It proposes regulatory measures to enforce fair pricing and wage standards, aiming to protect consumers and workers from exploitative practices.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and investigate issues related to cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. The board would coordinate oversight, provide guidance, and help improve national security and technology governance.
